newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares fall, further weakness seen.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares fall, further weakness seen.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell on Tuesday, pulled down by bank SKB as traders cashed in profits after the bank's recent jump on news that it planned a listing abroad.
Analysts said further weakness was likely to continue to the end of the week due to a lack of fresh foreign capital that was awaiting final election results.
"Brokers that bought SKB shares recently at a much lower price are now trying to take profits," one trader said.
The final unofficial election results show that the ruling centre-left Liberal Democrats would get 25 seats in the new 90 seat parliament.

However, the Liberal Democrats may have to hand over the government to the "Spring" alliance consisting of the rightist People's Party, centre-right Social Democrats and conservative Christian Democrats that are expected to get 45 seats.
Traders said shares may fall if "Spring parties" manage to form the government, due to their cautious stand towards Slovenia joining the European Union.
The 10-share SBI index fell 1.86 percent or 22.64 points to 1,196.2. Overall 13 shares fell, three rose and one remained unchanged, while seven were untraded.
Turnover rose to 533.9 million tolars from 205.4 million.
Bank SKB was the most active share, falling 2.22 percent or 1,000 tolars to 44,000 tolars on volume of 9,071 shares for total turnover of 397.6 million tolars.
"SKB could reach about 60,000 tolars on our bourse after it is listed on one of the foreign bourses," Toni Apollonio, an analyst at bank A told Reuters.
The bank last week said it planned to list its shares abroad in the near future. The bank's share holders are expected to vote on the proposal next week.
Brokerage Primofin was the day's leading decliner, falling 13.86 percent to 31,010 tolars on volume of 176 shares for total turnover of 5.7 million tolars.
Construction company GPG was the biggest gainer, surging 6.27 percent to 7,970 tolars on volume of 233 shares for total turnover of 1.8 million tolars.
